question: What is the minimum attendance required to appear for the end-semester examination?
answer: You must have a minimum of 75 per cent attendance in each course, computed separately for the theory and practical components, to be eligible to appear for the end-semester examination in that course. Attendance is calculated from the first day of instruction to the last instructional day and includes all lectures, tutorials, and practical sessions. If you fall below this and your shortage is not condoned, you will be detained and barred from appearing for the exam.

question: How are marks split between internal assessment and the end-semester exam for a theory course?
answer: For a theory course, the 100 marks are split into 40 marks for continuous internal assessment and 60 marks for the end-semester examination conducted by the Controller of Examinations. The 40 internal-assessment marks are further split into two mid-term tests of 15 marks each (held in the sixth and twelfth weeks) and 10 marks for assignments, quizzes or tutorials announced by the instructor in the first week of the semester.

question: What is the minimum I need to score to pass a course?
answer: To pass a course you must secure at least 30% of the marks in the end-semester examination AND at least 40% of the total marks (internal assessment plus end-semester examination combined). Failing either requirement results in an 'F' grade in that course.

question: What letter grade do I get for 85 marks?
answer: For 85 marks out of 100, you will receive the letter grade A+ (Excellent) with 9 grade points. According to the grading table, marks in the range 80 to 89 correspond to the A+ grade.

question: How many days do I have to apply for re-evaluation after results are declared?
answer: You have ten working days from the date of declaration of results to apply to the Controller of Examinations for re-evaluation of the answer script of a theory course, on payment of the prescribed fee per course. No application shall be entertained after this period, and re-evaluation is not available for practical examinations, project evaluations, or internal assessment.

question: What happens if I miss an end-semester exam because I was ill?
answer: If you miss an end-semester exam because of illness, you must submit a medical certificate issued by a registered medical practitioner and countersigned by the Institute Medical Officer to the Controller of Examinations within five working days of the date of the exam. If the certificate is accepted, you will be allowed to appear for the course in the next supplementary examination, that appearance will count as your first attempt, and you will be exempt from the supplementary examination fee.

question: What is the penalty if I am caught with a mobile phone in the exam hall?
answer: Possessing a mobile phone in the exam hall is treated as a first offence of unfair means. The penalty is that the examination in the concerned course is cancelled and you will be awarded grade F in that course; a second offence cancels all semester examinations (grade F in all courses), and a third offence results in expulsion from the Institute. The rule applies even if the phone is switched off.

question: What time do the hostel gates close at night?
answer: The hostel gates close at 10:30 p.m. every day. Residents who return after the gates close must sign the late-entry register maintained by the security staff and record the reason for the delay. The gates reopen at 5:30 a.m.

question: Can I use an induction cooktop in my hostel room?
answer: No, you cannot use an induction cooktop in your hostel room. The Hostel Handbook explicitly prohibits the use of induction cooktops in hostel rooms, and doing so will lead to confiscation of the appliance and a fine of Rs. 1,000 per occurrence.

question: How much is the late fee if I pay my semester fees after the due date?
answer: If you pay your semester fees after the due date, a late fee of Rs. 100 per day is charged up to and including the last date for that payment, and the late fee is capped at Rs. 1,500 for any single payment. For example, for the odd-semester tuition, examination and development fee, payment is due by 15 July 2026 and the last date to pay (with late fee) is 31 July 2026. No payment is accepted after that last date.

question: What is the last date to pay the odd semester tuition fee?
answer: The last date to pay the odd semester tuition fee (along with the examination and development fee) for 2026-27 is 31 July 2026. Payments after this date are not accepted, subject to the limited exception in Section 3.2 for documented education-loan or scholarship delays.

question: Who is eligible for the merit-cum-means scholarship?
answer: You are eligible for the Merit-cum-Means Scholarship if your annual family income from all sources does not exceed Rs. 3,00,000 and you have a CGPA of not less than 7.0 at the end of the preceding academic year (or, for first-year students, not less than 80 per cent marks in the qualifying examination). You must also submit an income certificate issued by a Tehsildar or an officer of equivalent rank that is not older than six months.

question: Do I get leave if there is a death in my family?
answer: Yes. If your parent, sibling, grandparent or spouse passes away, you are entitled to bereavement leave of up to seven days, and this period is counted as attendance. You should inform the HoD by e-mail or through the student portal before or during the leave, and submit a written application on return.

question: Will I get my hall ticket if I have not paid my tuition fees?
answer: No. If you have outstanding tuition fee dues on the last date of payment, the Institute shall not issue your hall ticket for the end-semester examination and shall not permit you to appear for it. However, your hall ticket will be released within one working day once the dues are cleared, provided the examination has not yet commenced.

question: How long can a break of study be?
answer: A break of study may be granted for one semester or one academic year, on medical grounds only, and cannot be granted more than once during the B.Tech. programme. The break must be certified by the Institute Medical Officer and approved by the Dean.

question: What is the maximum time allowed to complete the B.Tech programme?
answer: A student must complete all requirements of the B.Tech. programme within a maximum period of seven academic years from the date of first admission, failing which the student's name shall be removed from the rolls of the Institute.

question: Can I get a mess rebate if I go home for two weeks?
answer: Yes, you are entitled to a mess rebate for a two-week absence from the hostel. Under the Hostel Handbook, a resident absent for a continuous period of seven days or more is entitled to a rebate of mess charges for the period of absence, provided the absence is recorded in the leave register in advance and the rebate form is submitted within seven days of return. Two weeks clearly exceeds the seven-day minimum, so the rebate applies, subject to those procedural conditions.

question: How much medical insurance cover do students have?
answer: Every student is covered under the group medical insurance scheme of the Institute for hospitalisation expenses of up to Rs. 1,00,000 per year, and the premium is included in the development fee.

question: My attendance is 58% because I was hospitalised for three weeks. Can the shortage be condoned?
answer: The rulebook contradicts itself on this point. Clause 1 (AR §4.3) sets the minimum attendance for condonation at 65 per cent and states that below 65 per cent it 'shall not be condoned under any circumstances,' whereas Clause 2 (LM §2.2) sets the minimum at 55 per cent. These are incompatible thresholds for the same situation (medical condonation by the Dean). (Found by the corpus-wide audit, confidence 0.97.) Read on its own, AR §4.3 would give: No. Under AR §4.3, a shortage of attendance may be condoned by the Dean on medical grounds only if the student's attendance in the course concerned is not less than 65 per cent, and the rule expressly states that a shortage below 65 per cent 'shall not be condoned under any circumstances.' Since your attendance is 58%, you fall below this hard floor and the shortage cannot be condoned, notwithstanding your hospitalisation. As a consequence under AR §4.4, you may be detained in the course and awarded the grade 'DT'.
notes: escalated to conflict: the audit found AR §4.3 and LM §2.2 disagree; both were retrieved and AR §4.3 was cited

question: What is the lowest attendance percentage that can still be condoned on medical grounds?
answer: Two passages give incompatible thresholds for the lowest attendance percentage that may be condoned on medical grounds. LM §2.2 states that condonation may be granted provided attendance is 'not less than 55 per cent', while AR §4.3 requires attendance to be 'not less than 65 per cent' and declares that 'a shortage of attendance below 65 per cent shall not be condoned under any circumstances.' Because these clauses disagree on the very threshold asked about, the rulebook itself is inconsistent on this point.

question: If I withdraw my admission before classes begin, how much of my tuition fee will be refunded?
answer: The two passages give different answers for tuition-fee refund when a student withdraws before classes begin. [SF §6.2] says the refund is the tuition fee paid minus a ten per cent processing charge, so only 90% is refunded. [FS §4.1] says the refund is 100 per cent of the tuition fee paid for the semester. Because the rulebook itself disagrees on this specific point, I cannot tell you which one applies — you should check with the Accounts / Finance Office which schedule governs your case.

question: What CGPA do I need to maintain to keep my merit scholarship?
answer: Two passages give different CGPA thresholds for continuing the Merit Scholarship. [AR §11.2] requires a CGPA of not less than 7.5 at the end of each semester, while [SF §3.1] requires a CGPA of not less than 8.0 at the end of each semester. Because the Academic Regulations and the Scholarship and Fee Concession Policy state incompatible minimum CGPAs, you should clarify which policy applies in your case; the two clauses cannot be reconciled here.

question: What happens if I miss the end-semester exam because of a family wedding?
answer: The rulebook does not address what happens if you miss an end-semester exam because of a family wedding. The closest passage covers absence on medical grounds, not absence for personal or family events.

question: Can I get a re-test if I missed a mid-term test for a job interview?
answer: The rulebook does not address re-tests for missed mid-term tests due to a job interview. The closest passage, EE §3.3, covers re-tests only when a student misses a mid-term test on medical grounds and submits a medical certificate within five working days.

question: Can I change my branch after the first year?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a student may change their branch after the first year. The closest passage, AR §3.4, deals with adding or dropping a course within the first two weeks of a semester, not with a change of branch.

question: Is there a dress code for laboratory sessions?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether there is a dress code for laboratory sessions. The closest passage is EE §8.2, which deals only with the requirement to submit a certified laboratory record before appearing in the end-semester practical examination.

question: Can a day scholar eat in the hostel mess by paying per meal?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a day scholar (a student not residing in the hostel) may eat in the hostel mess on a per-meal payment basis. None of the passages deal with day scholars or with casual/per-meal access to the hostel mess. The closest passage, HH §4.1, only states that every resident must be a hostel mess member and that mess charges are paid in advance for the semester.

question: Are pets allowed in the hostel?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether pets are allowed in the hostel. The closest related passage lists other items and activities that are prohibited, such as gambling, loud music, firecrackers, posters on walls, and overnight guests, but it does not mention pets.

question: What is the fee for a duplicate identity card?
answer: The rulebook does not address the fee for a duplicate identity card. The closest passage mentions the Institute identity card as a required document for the examination hall, but does not specify any fee for replacing it.

question: Can I get academic credit for a summer internship?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a summer internship can be counted for academic credit. The closest passage, AR §2.2, only explains how credits are earned through courses (lectures, tutorials, practicals) and the minimum of 160 credits required for the B.Tech. degree.

question: Is there a scholarship for students from the EWS category?
answer: The rulebook does not address the question of a scholarship specifically for students from the EWS (Economically Weaker Section) category. The closest passage covers the Merit-cum-Means Scholarship, which is awarded on the basis of family income and academic performance, not EWS category.

question: Are grace marks given if I fail a course by one or two marks?
answer: The rulebook does not address the question of grace marks for students who fail a course by one or two marks. None of the passages mention grace marks, border-line marks, or any discretionary award of marks to students falling just short of the passing requirement. The closest passage addresses the converse situation: where the failure rate in an entire course exceeds forty per cent, moderation may be applied uniformly to that course.

question: Can I write my answers in Hindi instead of English in the end-semester exam?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether you may write your answers in Hindi instead of English in the end-semester examination. The closest passage provided covers the passing thresholds for the end-semester examination, not the permitted language of answer scripts.

question: What happens if there is a printing error in the question paper?
answer: The rulebook does not address what happens if there is a printing error in the question paper. The closest passage covers the interpretation of Regulations, stating that the Vice-Chancellor's decision is final on any interpretation question.

question: How do I get a duplicate degree certificate if I lose the original?
answer: The rulebook does not address the procedure for obtaining a duplicate degree certificate if the original is lost. The closest passage covers the prerequisite of obtaining a no-dues certificate before the original degree certificate can even be issued.

question: How many books can I borrow from the library at a time?
answer: The rulebook does not address how many books a student may borrow from the library at a time. The closest passage only states that a no-dues certificate from the Library is required before the Institute issues your degree certificate, consolidated grade card and transfer certificate.

question: What is the procedure to transfer to another university mid-course?
answer: The rulebook does not address the procedure for transferring to another university mid-course. The closest passage covers the process for withdrawing admission from the Institute, not transferring to another university.

question: Can I keep a two-wheeler in the hostel parking?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a resident may keep a two-wheeler in the hostel parking. The closest passage is HH §5.4, which lists prohibited activities and items such as gambling, loud music, firecrackers, wall writing, and overnight guests, but says nothing about vehicles in hostel parking.

question: Is there a fee concession if my sibling also studies at the institute?
answer: The rulebook does not address any fee concession on the basis of a sibling studying at the Institute. The closest passage covers a different category entirely — a concession for children of permanent employees of the Institute.

question: How do I get a bonafide student certificate for my bank loan?
answer: The rulebook does not address the procedure for obtaining a bonafide student certificate for a bank loan. The closest passage covers the no-dues certificate that a student must obtain before the degree certificate, consolidated grade card, and transfer certificate are issued.

question: What is the minimum CGPA to be eligible for campus placements?
answer: The rulebook does not address the minimum CGPA required for campus placements. None of the passages provided set a CGPA threshold for placement eligibility. The closest related passage, AR §3.3, addresses CGPA only in the context of credit-load limits, stating that students with a CGPA of 8.5 or above may register for up to 32 credits.

question: Can I re-appear in a course I have already passed to improve my grade?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a student who has already passed a course may re-appear in it to improve their grade. The closest provision, AR §9.1, covers re-evaluation of an existing answer script for students not satisfied with their end-semester marks, but not re-appearing in an already-passed course.

question: What happens if I fall ill in the middle of writing an exam?
answer: If you fall ill during an exam, you should inform the hostel supervisor or Warden immediately so that the Institute Health Centre (open 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.) or the on-call doctor/ambulance can attend to you. Note that the Examination Regulations also allow a missed mid-term test on medical grounds to be re-taken within two weeks of rejoining classes, provided you submit a medical certificate to the HoD within five working days of the test.

question: How do I get my name corrected on the grade card?
answer: The rulebook does not address the procedure for getting a name corrected on the grade card. The closest passage covers how the grade card itself is issued after the declaration of semester results.

question: Can I audit a course without earning credits?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a student can audit a course without earning credits. The closest passage, AR §1.2, simply defines a 'course' as one carrying a specified number of credits, but says nothing about auditing or non-credit participation.

question: Is there a discount if I pay the whole year's tuition fee in advance?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a discount is offered for paying the entire year's tuition fee in advance. The closest passage describes only the regular payment deadlines and the option to split a semester's fee into two equal instalments.

question: What is the punishment for plagiarism in a project report?
answer: The rulebook does not address the punishment for plagiarism in a project report. The closest passage covers unfair means in examinations generally, which are dealt with under the Examination and Evaluation Regulations.
